scientific limitations/integrity: Conditional consequence of Reider's exceptional dimension-one case. It gives necessary arithmetic, Hodge, and curve-theoretic restrictions only and does not assert existence or sufficiency for any positive integer \(m\). The primary theorem was checked in the source; the remaining deductions use Noether's formula, adjunction, and standard Kähler-surface identities.
title: Five-divisibility and a cubic-spin curve in Reider's exceptional branch
